x: Another to distinguish himself in an unorthodox way was Bob Glover who retired simply because he wanted to watch the leaders finish! Over the final lap the positions remained practically the same except that the gaps increased but Eric Gebbett, now getting fit again after a bout of gastro-enteritis, made up two places.
This race also saw the welcome return to racing of Bob Glover who finished 31st in an untroubled 33:38. Joe McDonald (42yrs) and Charlie Smart (55yrs) had a personal battle in this race.

A "ghost" Belgrave team ran in the Wimbledon '10' on the day of the Southern London-Brighton relay and finished 10th. Jack Brown was 27th in 55:18 Norman Stairs 36th in 56:17, Pete Sadler 38th in 56:23 and Bob Glover 46th in 57:12.

Bob Glover stepped into the breach to complete our scoring six, but his 89th actual position was too far back to get us anywhere in the team result, and our 7th position must have been a worst ever performance.

The only other change was O'Hara passing Black and moving up on Dabbs, who was not sorry to see the finish on this occasion. Of the others Chris Keavey and Bob Glover ran well and it was good to see Bob enjoying his racing once again.
Adrian Major was 50 yards clear of the field at one point but had to give way to the experienced'Valley'men, eventually finishing a good 5th, backed up closely in 7th place, by Bob Glover.

Fortunately, Bob Glover declined to go and by supporting our main fixture became a vital scorer in our league team. John Thresher produced a strong finish, passing two men in the last 100 yards, to be our first scorer in fourth place.

The versatile Lionel Mann added 3 miling to his repertoire (having already notched up a run in the Belgrave '20' and a 2:00.2 'half' this season) and it was pleasing to see Bob Glover, a little overweight maybe, out on the track again.
Undoubtedly the foul weather may have dissuaded some people from coming out, or perhaps the hefty figure of Bob Glover, on the door handling the takings, put some people off!!!

Don Maclean started about 12 minutes behind the feild but was unable to catch any tail-enders in the next 42 minutes. At least he must have enjoyed it more than Bob Glover and Peter Wrench who went off course and were not recorded in!

Of our other runners, and we had 25 out all together, the bouquets went to Bob Glover and Eric Penny. Bob was showing some of his old fire again and moved very well to finish 96th, and Eric continued his steady improvement to record a best ever placing of 118th.
Is this the gesture of comradeship that prompted the same authors to help Bob Glover when he was homeless, living in his car parked at a lonely copse somewhere in Surrey?
NOT FAIR that 'Little' Ian Gillings trains with the big boys - their pride wont let them 'drop' and Little Ian duffed up our aimiable giant Bob Glover round the Park (Battersea) the other day.

Peter Hilliar recovered well after considerable loss of ground in the middle stages whilst Bob Glover showed some excellent form. Those "old stagers" Charlie Walker and Arthur Bruce went round in tandem for most of the race with Chas. having the edge on the last circuit.

Bob Glover recently won his first race since he took up running 17 years ago - a 2 miles in 10:03 - shows what perseverence can do. He also won his first medals within the space of two weeks - Club '3' and '6' standards!

A polished effort that begins at the door where the Hollywood smile of our commissionaire Bob Glover slips one into gear for a roaring start, to the "Three Just Men", Tom, Frank and Norman dispensing the necessary with an expertise and assurance that would woo Dexter and his friends from the sordid bar of the Hilton.

…a completely new team and with Dick Piotrowski, John Dear, Roger Donnison, Lionel Mann, Malcolm Simms, Howard Satchell, Bob Glover and Pat O'Connor eligible we appeared to have a strong team but unfortunately Donnison, Mann, Simms and O'Connor were unable to appear and we lined up with a much deplet…
Also the indefatigable Bob Taylor and Gwen Cousins plus the welcome recruits Peter Hillier and friend, Philip Smith and friend and John Hall and Marjorie Pearson and Bob Glover.

Bob Glover, straight from his speed work on the track, showed he still had'nt lost his ability on the road with a very good run---he did'nt even say "That was hard" at the end so he must have felt good!

…ten yards in front of Bicourt and Major ... the second group now headed by Satchell, Dance and Donnison and at the back Bob Glover has gone in front of Tony Brooks whose recent success in the half has gone to his head ... and who is striking down the home straight like a champion? ...it's Thresher.…

Pat O'Connor maintained his recent good form for 10th and Bob Glover's 18th place was a particularly good effort. As usual the organisation went off smoothly and Gordon Biscoe deserves mention for handling yet another successful promotion
